newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, G7 agree on Chernobyl sarcophagus plan.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, G7 agree on Chernobyl sarcophagus plan.

text.p: Ukraine and its Group of Seven (G7) partners have agreed to a plan to stabilise the crumbling sarcophagus encasing the fourth reactor at the Chernobyl nuclear power station, the head of a G7 expert group said on Thursday.

"The G7 has agreed in our meetings that the shelter implementation plan agreed between Ukraine and the G7 is a cost-effective and efficient way to deal with this very important problem resulting from the 1986 accident at Chernobyl," Carol Kessler told a news conference.

"The project will run from now until at least the year 2005 and may cost as much as $780 million," Kessler said at a joint news conference with Ukrainian Environment Minister Yuri Kostenko following meetings between Ukrainian officials and G7 experts in the former Soviet republic this week.

Ukraine has demanded that the covering, feared to be leaking radiation after its hasty construction in the wake of the disaster 11 years ago, be stabilised as part of moves to close Chernobyl by 2000 in exchange for $3.1 billion in Western funding.

Kessler said the project included stabilising the structure's walls, building shields over fuel deposits still in the sarcophagus until they can safely be removed, and building some sort of shelter over it.

Ukraine estimates that 4,300 people have died since the April 26, 1986 disaster when Chernobyl's fourth reactor exploded, sending a radiation cloud over much of Europe. It was the world's worst nuclear accident.
